correctness.rationale: Exact reciprocal-equilibrium 2x2 system yields unique physically positive rational endemic fractions iff ab>gh, and source Theorem 3 supplies local stability. The sign difference has affine numerator Aδ+B with positive denominator, hence strict iff AB<0 and exactly one positive crossing. Explicit rational test rates and symbolic checker independently verify algebra; finite checks are not substituted for proof.

originality.rationale: The closest source gives general individual parameter monotonicity, existence and stability, but not a comparative group-ranking threshold for two cross-only groups. Its explicit formula uses homogeneous out-regular networks, not this heterogeneous full-rank contact matrix. Distinct two-patch migration, gradual-waning, and stochastic/global-stability papers inspected; Published-finding index searches returned related but mathematically distinct results. Residual historical priority uncertainty expressly identified.
residual_risks: Original 2026 arXiv v2 was read, but earliest public source date is documented by arXiv v1 metadata; an unrelated earlier public version of the *specific ranking theorem* may exist outside indexed search.
Full 2013 Muroya--Enatsu--Kuniya original and full Yang--Draief--Yang 2017 text unavailable here, leaving unexcluded subsumption in a broad theorem or appendix.
A generic parameterized multigroup SIRS closed-form family may contain the same two-group statement implicitly; source snippets and bounded indexed retrieval cannot establish priority.
The interpretation is a deterministic stylized model comparison; no clinical empirical inference.

value.rationale: Natural epidemiological question about which of two interacting communities has larger endemic infection burden when immunity wanes at a common rate. Supplies sharp necessary-and-sufficient crossing condition, at-most-one theorem, exact admissible reversal and symmetry impossibility boundaries. Distinguished from routine individual monotonicity and from nonmotivated parameter slices; does not claim empirical forecasting.
